solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hard decision to expel all but the last

parts.note: an umpire's or referee's call is a decision

indicators.note: tells us to keep every letter of the word for expel except its final one

parts.note: to oust someone is to expel them

explanation.surface: A tough ruling that throws everyone out except the last person standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' looks like the adjective for a difficult decision, but it is the definition; 'to' is a link, and 'all but the last' drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone emotionally unfeeling and insensitive to others' suffering.

clue.text: Maybe like chicken — or beef often — fine cuts

indicators.note: the fine letter cuts into the beef word

parts.note: corned beef is the common salted form
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Chicken or beef sold in fine portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like butchery, but it means the F breaks into CORNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry raised on maize grain are described this way, as are wholesome rural folk.

clue.text: Arm or leg unaffected after climbing exercise

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the limb

parts.note: each is a limb

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing reads upward, so the word for unaffected is reversed

parts.note: pure means unaffected, untainted

explanation.surface: An uninjured limb used after a climb.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means reading upwards, so the word is turned round; 'after' places it behind the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming up and stretching before activity is a phrasal verb for exercise.

clue.text: Old perjurer gives address, not right

indicators.note: the right letter is not there, so it is removed

parts.note: one who orates gives a speech or address

explanation.surface: A former liar makes a speech, which is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot of 1678 under oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The English conspirator who fabricated the Popish Plot is the most famous perjurer in history.

clue.text: Gave loans out for extended work?

indicators.note: out says the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lent money to fund a long project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extended' hints at the loans, but the work is a long book.
explanation.definitionFit: A long family novel, a multi-volume story, is an extended work of fiction.

clue.text: Pressure to stop mail while away

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the pressure letter goes into the word for mail to block it

parts.note: to mail a letter is to send it
P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone trying to hold back the post while they are on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'while away' looks like 'during an absence', but it is the verb phrase meaning to pass time.
explanation.definitionFit: To while away an afternoon is to pass or use up that time, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Crazy, say, having eight as answer?

indicators.note: having the crew as the answer means the crew takes the answer letter's place

parts.note: a rowing eight is its crew

explanation.surface: A mad question: is eight the solution?
explanation.walkthrough: In 'say', the A (answer) is swapped for CREW, a rowing eight; 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for mad, eccentric.

clue.text: Period preceding mock battle

parts.note: an eve is the time just before an event
a sham is a fake or mock thing

explanation.surface: A spell before a staged fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mock battle' looks like a phrase, but the definition is just 'battle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon de Montfort was killed in 1265 at the battle fought near this Worcestershire town.

clue.text: March the first in Newtown is ace!

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: Someone saying March's opening in Newtown was excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon at something is an expert, as an ace is.

clue.text: Article on this cricketer would be made into film

definitions.text: Article on this cricketer would be made into film

parts.words: Article on this cricketer would be made into film
parts.note: put the definite article before this fielding position and the title of a 1949 Carol Reed thriller appears

explanation.surface: A piece about a cricketer is to become a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, third man is a fielding position behind the slips; with 'The' it is a famous film starring Orson Welles.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder in that position on the off side is named after it, and with an article it is the film title.

clue.text: Without limits, that stuff is forbidden by religious law

indicators.note: removing the boundary letters of the word that leaves only its inner pair

parts.note: to stuff something is to ram or cram it in

explanation.surface: A remark that certain material, taken to extremes, is banned by faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without limits' strips the outer T's of 'that', leaving HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic law uses this Arabic term for anything prohibited, the opposite of halal.

clue.text: Great time for assembling task force

indicators.note: assembling puts parts together in a new arrangement, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A lovely occasion for gathering a working group together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great time' is anagrammed by 'assembling'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist group set up to tackle one particular problem, often testing security, is called a task force.

clue.text: Beams before sweet revenge starts

indicators.note: the revenge letter is placed before the dessert word
the start of the word revenge is its opening letter

parts.note: afters is British slang for the sweet or dessert course

explanation.surface: Wooden supports placed ahead of a sweet act of getting even.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British informal for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Roof timbers that slope from ridge to eaves are long beams.

clue.text: Admonitory words at different times?

definitions.meaning: a mild warning phrase said to calm or reprove someone
read literally, the present and a past moment, two separate times; as a phrase, occasionally

explanation.surface: Words of warning, delivered on several occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a gentle reproof, and its two words name two different points in time.

clue.text: Type of broadcasting agency to flourish

parts.note: a medium is an agency or means through which something is done
to flourish a sword or hand is to wave it

explanation.surface: A broadcasting organisation about to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: This radio band, with AM transmission, is one kind of broadcasting frequency range.

clue.text: Awfully mildewy around upper half of this plant

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the half word
awfully suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue the upper half is the first two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A plant covered in nasty mould.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'upper half' of a word is its first half, here two of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A low aromatic herb growing wild on heaths is this plant.

clue.text: Caliph's men keeping mum

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters keep or hold the mother word inside them

parts.note: OR is short for other ranks, ordinary soldiers as distinct from officers
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A caliph's servants hold their tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like 'silent', but it is a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The second caliph of Islam, who succeeded Abu Bakr, bore this name.

clue.text: Girl some toast for snaffling boy

indicators.note: snaffling means grabbing, so the toast word takes in the boy's name

parts.note: a round of toast is a slice or batch
Sam is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl offering toast to a boy who steals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Safe place to go to see massacre

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
loo is British informal for a toilet

explanation.surface: A secure spot from which to witness a slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is thieves' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1819 Manchester killing of protesters by cavalry is named after it.

clue.text: Frank, putting name forward, gets refusal …

indicators.note: putting, with forward, says a letter is shifted to a new place
with putting, says the name letter goes to the front

parts.note: open and frank both mean candid

explanation.surface: A man called Frank, giving his name first, is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but it is the adjective meaning candid; OPEN's N goes to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for no, a negative reply.

clue.text: Support, way down the bed, one hugging hooker?

parts.note: pit is slang for one's bed
in a rugby scrum each prop binds onto the hooker

explanation.surface: Someone lying in bed embracing a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' is the rugby position, flanked in the scrum by two props.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber beam holding up the roof of a mine shaft is a support far underground.

clue.text: …but has opposite response chasing OU belle, strangely

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the reply follows the anagram
strangely says the letters of the university and the belle come out in an odd new order

parts.note: the reverse of the refusal in the previous clue is a yes

explanation.surface: Someone saying yes to a beautiful Open University student, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Frank' in the clue before, linked by the dots: Frank Sinatra's nickname. The opposite of the previous clue's refusal is YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was nicknamed for his striking eyes, so the nickname stands for the singer.

clue.text: Called when hunting in harness, catching one cold

indicators.note: the harness word catches the two letters inside

parts.note: yoked animals are in harness
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A hunter calling while strapped in and catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox-hunting cry to urge hounds on, used as a verb, means shouted during the hunt.

clue.text: With a striking regularity?

parts.note: a clock chimes or strikes once every sixty minutes, a regular rhythm

explanation.surface: Something that happens remarkably often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like 'remarkable', but it is a clock chiming.
explanation.definitionFit: Clocks strike at each hour, so something done with that rhythm is done every sixty minutes.

clue.text: Place remote on display, by office

parts.note: things out are visible, on show
a post is a job or office

explanation.surface: Putting a distant site on show, beside a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement or military station far from the centre is a remote place.

clue.text: Some namedrop posh colleagues

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some posh people dropping names about colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal for a mate or colleague, from opposite number.

clue.text: Quietly curious about record company's charge

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: the word for curious wraps around the label's name

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
EMI is a well-known British record label

explanation.surface: A puzzled, soft-spoken question about what a record label charges.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance premium is the charge paid for cover, an extra sum levied.

clue.text: Old murder weapon, perhaps one concealed by Cluedo suspect

indicators.note: the numeral is hidden inside the suspect's name

parts.note: Professor Plum is one of the suspects in the board game Cluedo
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A historic weapon, possibly hidden by a suspect in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo (Clue in the US) is a murder-mystery board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman legionary's throwing spear was an ancient weapon that could kill.

clue.text: Painting of entrance catching the light

indicators.note: the doorway word catches and holds the beam inside it

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway or entrance
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A picture of a doorway lit up by the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction in paint, as a portrait or representation, is a painting.

clue.text: Organism we hear and see in the same way

indicators.note: says the word for the organism is spoken and a word sounding alike is entered

parts.note: a lichen is a composite organism of fungus and alga

explanation.surface: A living thing that perceives and listens identically.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare two things as similar is to regard them as alike.

clue.text: Damp spot holding naval officer back

indicators.note: the word for spot holds the turned officer inside

parts.note: to spot someone is to spy them

indicators.note: the officer's letters are turned around

parts.note: PO is a petty officer in the navy

explanation.surface: A wet place keeping a sailor in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damp' is an older sense of the answer, now mostly meaning sentimental; PO is a petty officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through or wet is an older sense alongside sentimental.

clue.text: Low dome reconstructed in timber

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shallow dome rebuilt in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood from the elm tree is one kind of timber.
